title: EXCLUSIVE: SK Hynix conditions new US factory on more US chip equipment exports to China, sources say
key_facts: Reuters, citing sources, reports SK hynix wants US approval to export US chipmaking equipment to China as a condition of investing in a new US factory.
The plan centres on Solidigm, SK hynix's US subsidiary, which would install extra equipment in unused space at the Dalian NAND flash plant in China to help fund a new US NAND plant.
Solidigm is reportedly considering an IPO as early as next year.
SK hynix told Reuters the Mod B installation is under US government authorisation and it is not seeking to expand capacity there; Solidigm declined to comment.

In September 2025 the US Commerce Department revoked special authorisations for SK hynix and Samsung; 2026 shipments were approved in December 2025 with quantity limits, and 2027 approval has not been issued.
Dalian uses equipment from Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA.
quote_evidence: The plan centers on Solidigm, SK hynix’s U.S. subsidiary, which aims to install additional equipment in unused space at the company’s NAND flash facility in Dalian, China.
SK hynix, however, told Reuters that equipment installation at Dalian’s Mod B facility is proceeding in consultation with and under authorization from the US government.
why_it_matters_hint: US limits on chip equipment for Chinese plants remain tight, so a trade of US investment for export approval would be a test case.
notes: Reuters original returned HTTP 401; read TrendForce account of the Reuters report. Unnamed sources; SK hynix disputes the capacity-expansion framing.
